questions.question: What does the VLOOKUP function do in MS-Excel ?
questions.questionHtml: What does the VLOOKUP function do in MS-Excel ?

options.text: Checks whether text is the same in one cell as in the next
options.html: Checks whether text is the same in one cell as in the next

questions.solution: VLOOKUP in MS-Excel searches for a specified value in the first column of a defined range and returns a value in the same row from another column within that range. It is used to retrieve data efficiently from structured tables by matching a lookup value. This function is especially helpful for managing large datasets.

questions.question: ______ devices are internal or external devices that connect directly to a computer but do not contribute to the computer's primary function, such as computing.
questions.questionHtml: ______ devices are internal or external devices that connect directly to a computer but do not contribute to the computer's primary function, such as computing.
questions.solution:
Option 1 is the correct answer i.e. Peripheral devices.

  • Except for CPU, motherboard, and Primary memory devices all most all devices are the peripheral devices.
  • CPU performs computation, memory stores the data to be processed as well as the information, therefore these cannot be termed as peripheral devices.
  • Peripheral devices, the devices which don't perform any basic computation, can be further classified into three types:
    • Input devices:
      • These devices are used to give instructions and enter data into the computer.
      • For eg.: Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner, mic etc.
    • Output Devices:
      • These devices give the information after the data is processed.
      • For eg.: Monitor, Speakers, Plotter etc.
    • Storage devices:
      • These devices store data and information on them.
      • Eg.: flash drives,

questions.question: What is the class of computer bugs, related to the formatting and storage of calendar data for dates beginning in the year 2000, known as?
questions.questionHtml: What is the class of computer bugs, related to the formatting and storage of calendar data for dates beginning in the year 2000, known as?
questions.solution: The class of computer bugs related to the formatting and storage of calendar data for dates beginning in the year 2000 is known as Y2K. These bugs were due to the practice of abbreviating a four-digit year to two digits, which caused issues when the year changed from 1999 to 2000.

questions.question: Identify whether the given statements are true or false. (i) Two consecutive cells in an MS Word table column cannot be merged. (ii) Two consecutive cells of an MS Word table row cannot be merged.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify whether the given statements are true or false.

(i) Two consecutive cells in an MS Word table column cannot be merged.

(ii) Two consecutive cells of an MS Word table row cannot be merged.
questions.solution:
The correct option is (4)

(I) False, (II) False

Key Points

  • A table's first and last cells cannot be combined. Just two or more consecutive rows or two adjacent columns may be combined. It is possible to merge two or more consecutive cells in a column.
  • A table heading that spans multiple columns can be made by horizontally merging numerous cells. Choose the cells you want to combine. Click Merge Cells in the Merge group under Table Tools on the Layout tab.
  • Click the merged cell, then select the left, center, or right alignment options adjacent to Merge & Center to merge the cells without centering the data.
  • Cells must be completely adjacent to one another, not just close by. If the selected cells cannot be combined, the Merge Cells button will be disabled or greyed out.

Additional Information Combine cells

  • Drag the pointer across the cells you want to combine in the table.
  • Go to the Layout tab on the ribbon.
  • Choose Merge Cells.

questions.question: _______ are motion effects that we can use when in Slide Show view add movement to slides as an advance from one slide to another to control speed and event.
questions.questionHtml: _______ are motion effects that we can use when in Slide Show view add movement to slides as an advance from one slide to another to control speed and event.

The correct answer is "Transition".

Key Points

  • Transitions: The animation effects specially used to introduce slides in a presentation is known as slide transition. It is also referred to as a motion effect that we can use when in Slide Show view add movement to slides as an advance from one slide to another to control speed and event. Some popular transition names are Fade, Push, Wipe, Random bars, Split and so on.

questions.question: The first mechanical computer designed by Charles Babbage was called?
questions.questionHtml: The first mechanical computer designed by Charles Babbage was called?
questions.solution: Charles Babbage designed the first mechanical computer called the Analytical Engine. It was a groundbreaking concept that laid the foundation for modern computing, featuring components such as an arithmetic logic unit, control flow through conditional branching and loops, and integrated memory.

questions.question: Identify whether the given statements related to the features of computer are true or false. a) Scalability: Computers' capabilities can be upgraded to meet demands. b) Emulation: Computers can simulate human emotions and empathy.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify whether the given statements related to the features of computer are true or false.

a) Scalability: Computers' capabilities can be upgraded to meet demands.

b) Emulation: Computers can simulate human emotions and empathy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a) true, b) false

Key Points

  • a) Scalability: Computers' capabilities can be upgraded to meet demands.
    • Explanation: Scalability refers to the ability of a system, network, or process to handle a growing amount of work or its potential to accommodate growth. Computers are designed to be scalable, meaning their hardware and software capabilities can be upgraded to meet increasing demands.
    • Verdict: True.
  • b) Emulation: Computers can simulate human emotions and empathy.
    • Explanation: Emulation in computing refers to the ability of a computer program or device to imitate another program or device. While computers can simulate certain behaviors and responses, they do not possess the ability to genuinely feel or emulate human emotions and empathy.
    • Verdict: False.

questions.question: Which of the following communication services is used to log on to a remote computer that is connected to the internet?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following communication services is used to log on to a remote computer that is connected to the internet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Telnet

Key Points

  • Telnet is a protocol used for remote login to a computer connected to the internet.
  • It allows users to execute commands on a remote machine as if they were using it locally.
  • Telnet operates in a client-server model, where the client accesses the server remotely.
  • It is mainly used for administrative purposes or accessing resources on a remote server.

Additional Information

  • Mailing Lists: Used for group communication via email but not for remote login.
  • Newsgroups: Provide forums for discussion but do not support remote computer access.
  • Internet Relay Chat: Enables real-time text communication but is not a remote login protocol.
  • Telnet Security: Telnet is not encrypted, so its usage is limited in modern systems due to security concerns.

questions.question: Digital signatures are based on which of the following cryptography?
questions.questionHtml: Digital signatures are based on which of the following cryptography?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Public key

Key Points

  • Digital signatures are a cryptographic technique used to verify the authenticity and integrity of digital data.
  • They are based on Public Key Cryptography, also known as asymmetric cryptography, which uses a pair of keys: a public key and a private key.
  • The private key is used to create the digital signature, while the public key is used to verify it.
  • Public Key Cryptography ensures that only the intended recipient can verify the authenticity of the message.

Additional Information

  • Private Key: This is used in symmetric cryptography where the same key is used for both encryption and decryption. It is not used in digital signatures.
  • Super Key: This term is used in database management systems to define a set of attributes that uniquely identify a record. It is unrelated to cryptography.
  • Foreign Key: This is a database concept used to link two tables. It is unrelated to cryptography or digital signatures.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for determining the best path for data packets using logical addresses?
questions.questionHtml: Which OSI layer is responsible for determining the best path for data packets using logical addresses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Network Layer.

Key Points

  • Network Layer is the third layer in the OSI model and is responsible for path determination and logical addressing.
  • It determines the best route for data packets to travel from the source to the destination using routing algorithms.
  • This layer uses logical addresses, such as IP addresses, to identify devices on a network.
  • It ensures end-to-end connectivity and manages traffic congestion by splitting data into packets.
  • Functions such as routing, addressing, and fragmentation are performed at the Network Layer.

Additional Information

  • Functions of the Network Layer:
    • Routing: Determines the best path for data to reach its destination.
    • Logical Addressing: Assigns IP addresses to devices for identification.
    • Packet Forwarding: Transfers packets from one network to another.
    • Fragmentation: Splits large data packets into smaller units for efficient transmission.
  • Protocols at the Network Layer:
    • IP (Internet Protocol): Provides logical addressing and routing.
    • ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol): Used for error reporting and diagnostics.
    • ARP (Address Resolution Protocol): Resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses.
    • RIP (Routing Information Protocol): A distance-vector routing protocol used for path determination.
  • Key Features:
    • Ensures data is delivered to the correct destination by choosing the most efficient path.
    • Provides logical separation between devices on a network using IP addresses.
    • Manages data traffic and prevents network congestion through efficient routing.
    • Ensures compatibility between different types of networks and devices.
  • Important Points:
    • The Network Layer operates independently of the physical devices and focuses on logical connectivity.
    • It is crucial for maintaining communication between devices in a large-scale network such as the internet.
    • Proper configuration of network layer protocols is essential for seamless data transfer and network security.

questions.question: What is the function of the cache memory in a computer's memory hierarchy?

options.html: To provide permanent storage for data and files.

options.text: To store frequently used data for faster access by the CPU.
options.html: To store frequently used data for faster access by the CPU.

options.text: To control the flow of data between the CPU and memory.
options.html: To control the flow of data between the CPU and memory.

options.text: To manage the allocation of memory resources to different programs.
options.html: To manage the allocation of memory resources to different programs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is To store frequently used data for faster access by the CPU. 

Key Points

The ability of cache memory to improve a computer's performance relies on the concept of locality of reference.

Locality of reference refers to the tendency of the computer program to access the same set of memory locations for a particular time period.

Cache memory creates a pattern in which CPU, While accessing or requesting data first checks with cache memory.

Let's analyze the options one by one.
 

Option 1-It's the correct answer as explained above.
 

Option 2- It's a concept of software engineering, which states that 90 % of program execution time is spent executing 10% of code.
 

Option 3- References do not cluster all the time. So, if they cluster also it's not guaranteed that the CPU will request the same cluster address.
